title: Suggestions View (Console) — Frontend Implementation Plan (Beta)
linked_artifacts: GitHub: redwood/pr-21957 (Console UI: add Suggestions view beta)
body:
Context
We’re shipping the beta “Optimization suggestions” experience in the Redwood Console. Scope is strictly batching + caching suggestions surfaced via Optimize Suggestions service.

This doc is the concrete frontend implementation plan for the Suggestions page: routing, component breakdown, data fetching/caching, pagination/sorting, and error/empty-state handling. It’s written to align with the backend API contract (stable IDs, cursor pagination) and the design spec (table list + details drawer).


0) Assumptions / inputs
- Feature flag: Suggestions view is gated per-org (and potentially per-project) via OptimizeSuggestionsBeta flag.
- Access control: Users also require RBAC permission optimize:suggestions:read. If flagged on but permission missing, show a clear access denied state (do not fall back to “no data”).
- API: GET /optimize/suggestions supports filtering, sorting, and pagination (cursor-based), returns stable suggestion IDs and stale_as_of timestamp.
- Design: Primary UI is a table-like list with filter chips + sort, and a right-side details drawer on row click.
- Telemetry: We emit impression/expand/dismiss/apply-click events with required properties (org_id, project_id, route_id, model, suggestion_id, suggestion_type, risk, confidence).


1) User journeys to support (MVP for beta)
1) Discover suggestions
- Entry point: Console left nav → Optimize → Suggestions (or deep link).
- Default query: last 7 days telemetry window (server-defined) and sort by estimated_savings_usd_per_day desc.

2) Inspect a suggestion
- Click a row to open details drawer.
- Drawer includes “Why we recommend”, assumptions, savings estimate ranges if provided, risk explanation, and “How to apply” deep link(s) to config.

3) Dismiss / apply
- Dismiss (UI-only action; record dismissal event; backend persistence optional in beta—see “Known gaps”).
- Apply: CTA opens relevant config page with query params pre-filled; we track “apply_click” (NOT auto-apply).

4) Handle no results / no telemetry / not enabled
- If API says insufficient telemetry or returns “eligibility reason”, show the corresponding empty state with setup CTA.


2) Routing + page composition
Routes
- New route: /console/:orgSlug/:projectSlug/optimize/suggestions
- Optional deep link to open drawer: /optimize/suggestions?suggestion_id=<id>
  - Behavior: page loads list; after list resolves, if suggestion_id is present and found, open drawer.
  - If suggestion_id not found in first page, attempt a direct fetch-by-id only if backend supports it; otherwise show toast “Suggestion not found or no longer available” and do not loop.

Feature flag guard
- Route-level guard: If org not enabled for OptimizeSuggestionsBeta, show “Beta access required” empty state with link to request access.
- If enabled but RBAC missing, show “Access denied” empty state with support/internal request link.


3) Component breakdown (proposed structure)
Page-level
- <SuggestionsPage />
  - Owns: URL state ↔ query state sync, data fetching orchestration, top-level empty/error rendering, and page-level telemetry (impression).
  - Children:
    - <SuggestionsHeader /> (title, subtitle, help link, staleness chip if needed)
    - <SuggestionsFiltersBar /> (filter chips, search, sort dropdown)
    - <SuggestionsTable /> (virtualized list, row actions, loading skeletons)
    - <SuggestionDetailsDrawer /> (open/close, fetch detail if needed)
    - <SuggestionsFooter /> (pagination controls + “results per page” only if we decide to expose limit)

Shared components
- <RiskBadge />: already implemented in shared UI library (uses design-approved colors + tooltip copy).
- <ConfidenceBadge />: simple pill, likely “High/Medium/Low” (copy from design spec).
- <MoneyDelta />: $/day + % formatting.
- <LatencyDelta />: p50/p95 delta formatting with “ms” and sign.

Data models (frontend types)
- SuggestionListItem
  - suggestion_id (stable)
  - suggestion_type (batching | caching)
  - route_id / route_name
  - model
  - estimated_savings_usd_per_day
  - estimated_savings_pct
  - latency_delta_p50_ms / latency_delta_p95_ms
  - risk_level (low | medium | high)
  - confidence_level (low | medium | high)
  - stale_as_of (timestamp)

- SuggestionDetails (for drawer)
  - includes all list item fields plus:
  - why_recommended (bullets)
  - assumptions (bullets)
  - guardrails (bullets)
  - recommended_config (human-readable + link targets)
  - inputs_snapshot (optional, if included by API; we will not render raw metrics unless designed)


4) Data fetching strategy (caching, pagination, debouncing)
Library
- Use existing Console standard data layer (React Query). If we’re already on TanStack Query v4, stick with it.

Query keys
- List query key should include org_id, project_id, filters, sort, and cursor.
  - suggestions:list:{org}:{project}:{filtersHash}:{sort}:{cursor}

Pagination
- Cursor-based pagination per ADR. Use React Query useInfiniteQuery unless design requires explicit page numbers.
- Proposed UX: “Load more” (infinite) OR paginated table with Next/Previous.
  - For beta, prefer Next/Previous with a visible cursor model to reduce surprise and keep row counts stable.
  - Implementation detail:
    - Keep “current cursor” in URL (e.g., ?cursor=<token>) only if required for shareability.
    - Otherwise keep cursors in memory to avoid leaking opaque cursor tokens into shared links.

Sorting
- Sort options per design ticket (expected):
  - Savings ($/day): desc (default), asc
  - Risk: low→high (or high→low; confirm)
  - Confidence: high→low
  - Latency impact p95: asc
- Sorting triggers a full list refetch; reset cursor.

Filtering
- Filters (beta baseline):
  - suggestion_type (batching/caching)
  - risk_level
  - route (multi-select, optional)
  - model (multi-select, optional)
  - region (only if supported by API; otherwise omit)
- Filter changes are debounced (300ms) for text search; immediate for chip toggles.
- Filter state is mirrored to URL query params for shareability.

Caching
- Stale time: 60s for list. This avoids refetching on quick nav or drawer open.
- Refetch on window focus: disabled for this page (we don’t want background refetch to reorder table while user is reading). Provide manual refresh button in header.
- Manual Refresh
  - Button: “Refresh” → invalidates list query and refetches.
  - If API includes stale_as_of, we display “As of <time>” and update on refresh.

Drawer data
- Option A (preferred): list response includes enough detail for drawer (why/assumptions) so drawer doesn’t need a second request.
- Option B: drawer fetches details on open via /optimize/suggestions/{id}.
  - If we don’t have a details endpoint in v0, keep it all in list response.
  - If details endpoint exists, we still pass list item into drawer immediately (optimistic render), then hydrate extra fields.


5) Table rendering + performance
- Use row virtualization if >100 rows is common; otherwise keep it simple for beta.
- Use skeleton rows while loading.
- Row click opens drawer; provide secondary actions in kebab menu (Dismiss) to avoid accidental dismissal.
- Accessibility
  - Table must support keyboard navigation: arrow keys optional; tab to row; Enter opens drawer.
  - Drawer trap focus; Esc closes drawer.
  - Risk badge tooltip accessible via keyboard.


6) Empty states and how we determine them
We need to disambiguate:
A) Feature not enabled
- Condition: flag false for org/project.
- UI: “Optimization suggestions beta is not enabled for this org.” CTA: “Request access” (link to internal form or docs).

B) Access denied (RBAC)
- Condition: API returns 403 with known error code OR permissions endpoint indicates missing optimize:suggestions:read.
- UI: “You don’t have access to view suggestions.” CTA: “Request access” (link to internal support/INT ticket form).

C) Insufficient telemetry / not eligible
- Condition: API returns 200 with eligibility_status = insufficient_telemetry OR empty list + reason.
- UI: “Not enough telemetry yet” with:
  - what signals are required (QPS, cache metrics, latency histograms)
  - typical time to populate (e.g., “within 24 hours after enabling telemetry”)
  - CTA to telemetry setup page.

D) No suggestions available (healthy)
- Condition: API returns 200, eligible, but suggestions list empty.
- UI: “No suggestions right now” with explanation (“We didn’t find safe batching/caching changes with meaningful savings.”) and link to docs.

E) Backend error
- Condition: 5xx / network errors.
- UI: error panel with retry, status page link, and error request id (if present).

F) Stale estimates
- Condition: stale_as_of older than threshold (e.g., >48h) OR compute lag flag.
- UI: show warning banner “Estimates may be out of date (as of …).” Provide refresh; do not block.


7) Error handling details
- If list fetch fails:
  - Render error state at page level.
  - Include “Retry” button.
  - Log error to client error reporting with route, org/project ids, HTTP status, request id.

- If drawer hydration fails (Option B):
  - Keep drawer open; show inline “Couldn’t load full details” with Retry.
  - Still allow Apply CTA if we have enough info.

- If apply deep link destination not available (config page missing or route disabled):
  - Fallback: open docs page and show toast “Couldn’t open settings automatically. See docs.”


8) URL state (shareable + stable)
Query params (proposed)
- type=batching|caching (multi allowed: type=batching&type=caching)
- risk=low|medium|high (multi allowed)
- model=<string> (multi allowed)
- route_id=<id> (multi allowed)
- sort=savings_usd_per_day_desc (enum)
- suggestion_id=<id> (for drawer)

Rules
- Changing filters/sort clears suggestion_id to avoid stale drawer state.
- Closing drawer removes suggestion_id from URL.


9) Telemetry instrumentation (frontend)
Events (names per taxonomy doc; final names owned by Telemetry team)
- suggestions_view_impression
  - fired once when page renders and flag+rbac allow view.
  - props: org_id, project_id, default_sort, filters_applied_count

- suggestions_row_open
  - fired on drawer open (not on mere row focus).
  - props: suggestion_id, suggestion_type, route_id, model, risk_level, confidence_level, rank_position

- suggestions_dismiss_click
  - fired when user clicks Dismiss in row/drawer.
  - props: suggestion_id, reason_selected (if we add a reason modal; optional)

- suggestions_apply_click
  - fired when user clicks Apply CTA.
  - props: suggestion_id, destination (e.g., caching_config), opened_in_new_tab (bool)

Guardrails
- Do not emit prompt content or request payloads.
- Keep route identifiers consistent with existing Console route naming.


10) Testing plan (frontend)
Unit/integration (React Testing Library)
- Renders table with data, sorts correctly (client just changes query; ensure query param updates).
- Filter chips update URL and trigger refetch.
- Drawer open/close updates suggestion_id param.
- RBAC denied state renders on 403.
- Insufficient telemetry empty state renders on eligibility code.

E2E (Playwright; aligns with Leila’s checklist)
- Flag off → beta access empty state.
- Flag on + RBAC missing → access denied.
- Eligible + results → list loads, drawer opens, apply click navigates.
- Eligible + no results → “No suggestions right now”.
- API 500 → error with retry.
- Pagination: next/prev returns stable results; no duplicate keys; scroll position preserved.

Visual regression
- Risk badge colors and tooltip contrast (DES-669).


11) Rollout / operational notes (frontend impact)
- Page and components behind feature flag; do not ship nav entry to all users until flag rollout.
- Add “Beta” label on nav item and page header.
- Support “kill switch” behavior: if API health degrades, we can hide nav entry and render fallback empty state.


12) Open questions / decisions needed
- Pagination UX: Next/Previous vs infinite scroll. (I propose Next/Previous for beta stability.)
- Do we need a details endpoint? If not, we must include drawer copy fields in list response (bigger payload; check performance budget).
- Should “Dismiss” persist (server-side) or be session-only for beta? If server-side, confirm API contract.
- Which filters make beta (route/model vs just type/risk)? Design wants route/model; API readiness needs confirmation.
- staleness threshold and copy: coordinate with Applied ML (Sana/Maya) so UI language matches estimator guarantees.


13) Implementation checklist (sequenced)
1) Add route + feature flag guard + RBAC handling.
2) Implement query param state model (filters/sort/suggestion_id).
3) Implement list query + table skeletons.
4) Implement drawer open/close + details rendering.
5) Implement empty/error states per spec.
6) Add telemetry events + verify in dev dashboard.
7) Add E2E tests (RBAC, empty, pagination, error).
8) Perf pass: payload size, render time, virtualization decision.
9) Ship behind flag; dogfood with internal org(s).


Known gaps (explicitly out of scope for beta)
- Quantization suggestions UI.
- Auto-apply/rollout workflows.
- Customer-specific savings commitments or billing reconciliation in UI (we only show estimates + assumptions).

Notes to self
- Ensure suggestion_id is used as React key (stable). Avoid index keys.
- Prefer server-driven sorting; do not implement client-side sorting (risk of mismatch with pagination/cursor).
- Keep error states differentiated; “insufficient telemetry” should never show for 403.
